protected_scheduled_posts.hook: Spot the herd.
The moon drifts about 3.8 centimeters farther from Earth every year.
Butterflies taste with their feet. Sensors on their legs tell them when they've landed on the right plant.
Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us. The sunrise you see already happened a few minutes ago.
Snakes shed their skin in one piece, often turned inside out, several times a year as they grow.
Cats can't taste sweetness. They're drawn to fish for the protein, not the flavor.
Studies show honeybees can learn to recognize human faces.
Olive trees can live for more than a thousand years, and some of the oldest still bear fruit.
Giant pandas spend about half of every day eating bamboo.
Raindrops aren't shaped like tears. Small ones are round, and larger ones flatten out as they fall.
A daisy is really hundreds of flowers in one. Each speck in the yellow center is its own tiny bloom.
Cats sleep between 12 and 16 hours a day, ideally somewhere warm.
Most of the stars you can see at night are bigger and brighter than our sun.
Every rainbow is a full circle. From the ground, the horizon hides the bottom half.
Many flowers carry ultraviolet patterns we can't see, which guide bees straight to the nectar.
A group of cats is called a clowder.
Ferns are older than the dinosaurs. They first appeared more than 350 million years ago.
In Japan, the cherry blossom forecast is tracked across the country like the weather.
Bees see ultraviolet light, so to them a daisy looks like a target pointing to its center.
Cats have about 50 vertebrae in their spine. We have 33. That's how they stretch like this.
A chickadee can remember thousands of spots where it hid seeds for winter.
Twilight comes in three stages: civil, nautical and astronomical. Each one is a little darker.
Moonflowers open at dusk and close by morning. Night moths do the pollinating.
Cats can see in about one sixth of the light we need.
